author: reek
body: A render target can be pointed at a rectangle INSIDE a larger panel, by offsetting its base address while keeping the panel's own stride. That is what keeps a desktop's sidebar and taskbar on the glass around a moving 3D view, and the risk is the whole of it: get it wrong by one and the scene shears across the chrome, which on real hardware looks like a corrupt display rather than a wrong number.

author: reek
body: The subject here is `r3d-target-at`, not GopScene. GopScene reached the pane this way until 2026-07-30 and now renders into a back buffer and blits, so its own path is covered by `gop-scene-backbuffer` and this file covers the primitive underneath both.

author: reek
body: So this renders into a scratch panel pre-filled with a sentinel and asks where the pixels landed. The sidebar columns and the taskbar rows must still hold the sentinel and the content pane must not, on the same frame. Checking only that the content changed would pass just as well with a renderer that painted the entire panel.

author: reek
body: Counts sentinel pixels inside an arbitrary rectangle of the panel, so the same helper can ask about the sidebar, the taskbar and the content.
